_meta.about: Batch 011: D2C, food, consumer, logistics and lending companies. Leaders not re-checked on the web for this batch because the search budget ran out early; profiles carry an honest as_of. Listing status for Wakefit, Shadowfax and Shiprocket verified.
_meta.review: All entries unreviewed until the founder approves them.

companies.name: FreshToHome

parts.SELLS: FreshToHome sells fresh fish, seafood, chicken and mutton online, promising chemical-free meat with no preservatives. It also sells marinated ready-to-cook items, eggs and some groceries. Buyers are city households ordering through its app and website, and it supplies other retailers too.
parts.EARNS: It earns the margin between what it pays fishermen, farmers and suppliers and what customers pay. Buying directly from fishing harbours and running its own processing centres cuts middlemen. Fish and seafood are the heart of the business, and big southern cities are its strongest markets.
parts.SIZE: One of India's largest online sellers of fresh fish and meat, alongside Licious. It runs processing and delivery operations in several large Indian cities and has also worked in the Gulf region.
parts.RIVALS: Licious is its closest rival. It also competes with quick-commerce apps such as Blinkit, Zepto and Swiggy Instamart, with BigBasket, and with neighbourhood butchers and fish markets.
parts.WATCH: Watch whether it can turn steadily profitable while keeping cold chains tight, how it handles competition from quick-commerce apps that now stock fresh meat, and how far it grows its own processing capacity.

quiz.prompt: What is FreshToHome's core product category?
How does FreshToHome cut out middlemen?
options: By buying directly from harbours and farmers

quiz.prompt: Which company is FreshToHome's closest online rival?

companies.note_30w: FreshToHome sells chemical-free fish and meat online, buying straight from harbours and farms. It rivals Licious and quick-commerce apps. Watch profitability and cold-chain discipline.

companies.name: Haldiram's

parts.SELLS: Haldiram's sells namkeen such as bhujia and mixtures, sweets like soan papdi and rasgulla, ready-to-eat meals, frozen foods and biscuits. It also runs restaurants serving Indian snacks and meals. The Delhi and Nagpur family businesses were combined into one snacks company, which brought in outside shareholders in 2025.
parts.EARNS: Most money comes from packaged namkeen and sweets sold through kirana stores, supermarkets, e-commerce and quick-commerce apps. Restaurants and exports add to revenue. Traditional namkeen is the largest and most important category.
parts.SIZE: India's largest maker of packaged namkeen and one of the country's best-known food brands. Its products reach shops across India and Indian communities in many countries abroad.
parts.RIVALS: Bikaji Foods, PepsiCo's Lay's and Kurkure, ITC's Bingo, Balaji Wafers, Prataap Snacks and many regional namkeen makers compete for the same snack shelf.
parts.WATCH: Watch how the combined company integrates its Delhi and Nagpur operations, how new outside shareholders shape its plans, and whether it moves towards a stock market listing, which has been widely discussed.

quiz.prompt: Which product category is Haldiram's best known for?
Which listed company is a direct namkeen rival to Haldiram's?
Which businesses were combined into one Haldiram's snacks company?
options: Its Delhi and Nagpur family businesses

companies.note_30w: Haldiram's is India's largest packaged namkeen maker, also selling sweets and running restaurants. Its Delhi and Nagpur businesses combined into one company. Rivals include Bikaji and PepsiCo.

companies.name: Parle Products

parts.SELLS: Parle Products makes biscuits and confectionery, led by Parle-G glucose biscuits. Other brands include Monaco, Krackjack, Hide & Seek, Milano and Happy Happy biscuits, plus Melody, Mango Bite and Kismi sweets. It sells to households across India, especially in small towns and villages.
parts.EARNS: It earns by selling huge volumes of low-priced packs through a vast network of distributors and kirana stores. Margins per pack are thin, so scale matters. Biscuits are by far its largest category, with Parle-G as the anchor brand.
parts.SIZE: One of India's largest biscuit makers and among the most widely distributed food companies in the country. Parle-G is often described as one of the world's best-selling biscuit brands.
parts.RIVALS: Britannia is its main rival, with Good Day, Marie Gold and Tiger. ITC's Sunfeast, Mondelez's Oreo and Cadbury, Anmol, Priyagold and regional bakeries also compete.
parts.WATCH: Watch how it handles swings in wheat, sugar and palm oil costs, its push into premium biscuits and snacks, and competition for shelf space on quick-commerce apps.

quiz.prompt: Which is Parle Products' best-known biscuit brand?
Why does scale matter so much to Parle Products?
options: Its packs are low-priced with thin margins

quiz.prompt: Which company is Parle Products' main biscuit rival?

companies.note_30w: Parle Products makes Parle-G, Monaco, Krackjack and Melody, selling cheap packs in huge volumes through kirana stores. Britannia is its main rival. Watch input costs and premium push.

companies.name: Amul (GCMMF)

parts.SELLS: Amul is the brand of the Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation, owned by milk unions of Gujarat dairy farmers. It sells milk, butter, ghee, cheese, curd, paneer, ice cream, chocolates and protein products. It is not a listed company; farmers own it through their cooperatives.
parts.EARNS: GCMMF markets products made by member unions and passes most of what consumers pay back to farmers as milk prices. Liquid milk is its largest product, while butter, ghee, cheese and ice cream carry better margins.
parts.SIZE: India's largest dairy brand and one of the largest dairy cooperatives in the world. Its products are sold nationwide and exported to many countries.
parts.RIVALS: Mother Dairy, Nestle India, Hatsun Agro, Heritage Foods, Karnataka's Nandini, Britannia in cheese, and Hindustan Unilever's Kwality Wall's in ice cream compete with Amul.
parts.WATCH: Watch its expansion into new states and abroad, including fresh milk in the US, its push into protein and organic products, and how it balances farmer milk prices with consumer prices.

quiz.prompt: Who owns Amul?
What is Amul's largest product?
Which of these is a dairy rival to Amul?

companies.note_30w: Amul is India's largest dairy brand, owned by Gujarat dairy farmers through cooperatives. It sells milk, butter, cheese and ice cream. Rivals include Mother Dairy and Nandini.

companies.name: Balaji Wafers

parts.SELLS: Balaji Wafers makes potato chips, namkeen and extruded snacks under the Balaji brand, including wafers in many flavours, bhujia, chevda and puffs. It is a family-run company that sells mostly in western and central India, at low prices aimed at mass buyers.
parts.EARNS: It earns by selling large volumes of affordable snack packs through distributors and kirana stores. Keeping costs low through its own factories and potato sourcing lets it price below national brands. Potato wafers are its largest product.
parts.SIZE: One of India's largest regional snack makers and a market leader in Gujarat. It is often cited as a regional brand that holds its own against multinational chip makers in its home markets.
parts.RIVALS: PepsiCo's Lay's and Kurkure, ITC's Bingo, Haldiram's, Bikaji Foods, Gopal Snacks and Prataap Snacks compete with Balaji.
parts.WATCH: Watch its expansion beyond its core western markets, any new factories, and reports of large food companies and funds seeking a stake in the family business.

quiz.prompt: What is Balaji Wafers' largest product?
In which state is Balaji Wafers a market leader?
Which multinational chip brand competes with Balaji?

companies.note_30w: Balaji Wafers is a Rajkot family company selling cheap potato chips and namkeen, strongest in western India. It competes with Lay's, Bingo and Haldiram's. Watch expansion beyond Gujarat.

companies.name: Bikaji Foods

parts.SELLS: Bikaji Foods makes Bikaneri bhujia, namkeen, papad, packaged sweets like rasgulla and soan papdi, and western snacks such as chips. It sells under the Bikaji brand to households across India and to Indian communities abroad. It listed on the stock exchanges in 2022.
parts.EARNS: It earns by selling packaged snacks through distributors, modern trade and online channels. Ethnic namkeen and bhujia make up most of its revenue. Its home states such as Rajasthan, Assam and Bihar are its strongest markets.
parts.SIZE: One of India's largest ethnic snack makers and among the biggest producers of Bikaneri bhujia. It is a leading packaged snack brand in its core states.
parts.RIVALS: Haldiram's is its main rival. PepsiCo's Kurkure and Lay's, ITC's Bingo, Balaji Wafers, Prataap Snacks and Gopal Snacks also compete.
parts.WATCH: Watch its push into new states, frozen foods and quick-service outlets, its acquisitions of regional brands, and how it manages edible oil and grain costs.

quiz.prompt: Which snack is Bikaji best known for?
Where is Bikaji Foods headquartered?
Which company is Bikaji's main namkeen rival?

companies.note_30w: Bikaji Foods sells Bikaneri bhujia, namkeen, papad and sweets, strongest in Rajasthan, Assam and Bihar. Listed in 2022, it competes with Haldiram's. Watch expansion into new states.

companies.name: Wow! Momo

parts.SELLS: Wow! Momo runs quick-service restaurants selling momos, including steamed, fried and pan-fried versions. It also runs Wow! China for Chinese food and Wow! Chicken, and sells packaged frozen momos in shops. Young city diners are its main customers.
parts.EARNS: It earns from food sold in its outlets and kiosks, plus delivery orders through Zomato and Swiggy. Momos are its largest and best-known product line. Packaged frozen food is a smaller but growing business.
parts.SIZE: One of India's largest momo restaurant chains, with outlets in many Indian cities, especially in malls, airports and high streets.
parts.RIVALS: It competes with quick-service chains such as McDonald's, Domino's, Burger King and KFC, with Rebel Foods brands, and with countless local momo stalls.
parts.WATCH: Watch its expansion into smaller cities, the growth of its packaged frozen momos, and its moves towards profitability.

quiz.prompt: What food is Wow! Momo mainly known for?
Which smaller business is Wow! Momo growing alongside its restaurants?
Which cloud-kitchen company competes with Wow! Momo?

companies.note_30w: Wow! Momo runs momo-focused quick-service restaurants and sells frozen momos in shops. It rivals McDonald's, Domino's and street stalls. Watch smaller-city expansion and profitability.

companies.name: Chaayos

parts.SELLS: Chaayos runs tea cafes that serve customised chai, letting customers pick milk, sugar and spice options, along with Indian snacks such as samosas and vada pav. It also sells packaged tea online. Office-goers and students are its core customers.
parts.EARNS: It earns from beverages and food sold in its cafes and through delivery apps. Chai is its main product and carries strong margins compared with food. Delhi NCR, Mumbai and Bengaluru are its main markets.
parts.SIZE: One of India's largest tea cafe chains, with cafes across several big cities.
parts.RIVALS: Chai Point and Chai Sutta Bar are direct tea cafe rivals. Coffee chains such as Starbucks, Third Wave Coffee, Blue Tokai and Cafe Coffee Day compete for the same cafe visits.
parts.WATCH: Watch its cafe expansion, its moves towards profitability, and growth in packaged tea and delivery.

quiz.prompt: What is Chaayos' main product?
Which of these is a direct tea cafe rival to Chaayos?
Which product carries strong margins for Chaayos?

companies.note_30w: Chaayos runs tea cafes serving customised chai and Indian snacks in big cities. It rivals Chai Point and coffee chains like Starbucks. Watch expansion and profitability.

companies.name: Third Wave Coffee

parts.SELLS: Third Wave Coffee runs specialty coffee cafes serving espresso drinks, cold brews and food. It also sells roasted coffee beans and merchandise. Its customers are young urban professionals and students, mostly in large cities.
parts.EARNS: It earns mainly from beverages and food sold in its cafes, plus delivery orders and packaged coffee. Coffee drinks are the largest and highest-margin part of sales. Bengaluru is its strongest market.
parts.SIZE: One of India's fastest-growing specialty coffee chains, with cafes across several large cities, though smaller than Tata Starbucks.
parts.RIVALS: Tata Starbucks, Blue Tokai, Cafe Coffee Day, Costa Coffee, Barista and Chaayos compete for urban cafe customers.
parts.WATCH: Watch its new leadership team's push for profitability, the pace of new cafe openings, and how it handles rising rents and coffee bean costs.

quiz.prompt: What does Third Wave Coffee mainly sell?
Which city is Third Wave's strongest market?
Which of these is a Third Wave rival?

companies.note_30w: Third Wave Coffee runs specialty coffee cafes, strongest in Bengaluru. It competes with Starbucks, Blue Tokai and Cafe Coffee Day. Watch profitability and cafe expansion.

companies.name: Blue Tokai Coffee

parts.SELLS: Blue Tokai roasts Indian specialty coffee sourced from estates in Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu. It sells roasted beans and ground coffee online and in stores, and runs its own cafes. It also sells brewing equipment and has opened cafes abroad.
parts.EARNS: It earns from cafe sales of coffee and food and from packaged beans sold online, in supermarkets and on quick-commerce apps. Cafes bring in most of its revenue, while packaged coffee builds the brand at home.
parts.SIZE: One of India's best-known specialty coffee roasters and a leading homegrown cafe chain, with cafes in many Indian cities.
parts.RIVALS: Third Wave Coffee, Tata Starbucks and Cafe Coffee Day compete in cafes. In packaged coffee it faces Sleepy Owl, Nestle's Nescafe, Tata Coffee and Rage Coffee.
parts.WATCH: Watch its cafe expansion in India and overseas, including Japan, and how it handles volatile global coffee prices.

quiz.prompt: Where does Blue Tokai source its coffee?
Which part brings in most of Blue Tokai's revenue?
Which packaged coffee brand competes with Blue Tokai?

companies.note_30w: Blue Tokai roasts Indian specialty coffee, selling beans online and running cafes in India and abroad. It rivals Third Wave and Starbucks. Watch overseas cafes and coffee prices.

companies.name: Sleepy Owl

parts.SELLS: Sleepy Owl sells ready-to-drink and easy-brew coffee: cold brew packs, instant coffee, hot brew bags and canned coffee. It started as a direct-to-consumer brand online and now sells in supermarkets, quick-commerce apps and cafes.
parts.EARNS: It earns by selling packaged coffee through its own website, marketplaces like Amazon, quick-commerce apps and retail stores. Instant and cold brew products are its main lines, and online channels remain a big share of sales.
parts.SIZE: One of India's best-known direct-to-consumer coffee brands, though much smaller than mass instant coffee brands.
parts.RIVALS: Nestle's Nescafe and Hindustan Unilever's Bru dominate instant coffee. Rage Coffee, Blue Tokai, Continental and Tata Coffee also compete.
parts.WATCH: Watch its push into offline retail and quick-commerce, new product launches such as ready-to-drink cans, and its path to profitability.

quiz.prompt: Which product does Sleepy Owl sell?
Which big brand dominates instant coffee against Sleepy Owl?
Where did Sleepy Owl start selling?

companies.note_30w: Sleepy Owl sells cold brew, instant and canned coffee, first online and now in shops. It competes with Nescafe, Bru and Rage Coffee. Watch offline retail growth.

companies.name: The Whole Truth

parts.SELLS: The Whole Truth sells protein bars, peanut butter, protein powder, muesli, dark chocolate and snack bars marketed as having no added sugar or hidden ingredients. Its pitch is clean labels with ingredients listed upfront. Health-conscious urban shoppers are its buyers.
parts.EARNS: It earns by selling packaged foods through its website, Amazon, quick-commerce apps and supermarkets. Protein bars and protein powders are its most important categories. Online and quick-commerce channels bring in much of its sales.
parts.SIZE: One of India's fastest-growing health food brands and a leader among clean-label protein snack startups.
parts.RIVALS: Yoga Bar from ITC, RiteBite Max Protein, Pintola, MuscleBlaze, Super You and Mars-owned brands compete in protein snacks.
parts.WATCH: Watch its expansion into offline stores and new categories, and how stricter food labelling rules from FSSAI affect a brand built on label transparency.

quiz.prompt: What is The Whole Truth's core pitch?
options: Clean labels with no hidden ingredients

quiz.prompt: Which ITC-owned brand competes with The Whole Truth?
Which regulator's labelling rules matter for The Whole Truth?

companies.note_30w: The Whole Truth sells clean-label protein bars, peanut butter and protein powder, mainly online. It competes with Yoga Bar and RiteBite. Watch offline expansion and labelling rules.

companies.name: Paper Boat (Hector Beverages)

parts.SELLS: Hector Beverages sells Paper Boat drinks inspired by traditional Indian flavours such as aam panna, jaljeera, kokum and aamras, plus juices, coconut water and snacks like chikki. Its packaging and ads play on nostalgia. Urban families and young adults are its buyers.
parts.EARNS: It earns by selling packaged drinks and snacks through stores, supermarkets, online and quick-commerce apps. Ethnic and fruit drinks are its largest line, and summer is its biggest season.
parts.SIZE: One of India's best-known homegrown packaged drinks brands, though far smaller than cola and juice giants.
parts.RIVALS: Coca-Cola's Maaza and Minute Maid, PepsiCo's Slice and Tropicana, Dabur's Real, Raw Pressery and Reliance's Campa compete with Paper Boat.
parts.WATCH: Watch its push for profitability, wider distribution in smaller towns, and competition from cheaper drinks like Campa.

quiz.prompt: What is Paper Boat's main product?
Which juice brand is a Paper Boat rival?
What is Paper Boat's biggest season?

companies.note_30w: Paper Boat sells drinks built on traditional Indian flavours like aam panna and jaljeera. It competes with Maaza, Real and Campa. Watch profitability and small-town reach.

companies.name: Bira 91

parts.SELLS: Bira 91, run by B9 Beverages, makes craft-style beers such as Bira 91 White, Blonde and Boom, and runs taprooms. It sells in bars, restaurants and liquor stores. Young urban drinkers are its core buyers.
parts.EARNS: It earns by selling beer to state distributors, retailers and bars, with each state controlling licences and prices. Wheat beer and lager are its main lines, and big states with open liquor markets matter most.
parts.SIZE: One of India's best-known craft beer brands, though much smaller than the market leaders.
parts.RIVALS: United Breweries, which owns Kingfisher and Heineken, dominates. Carlsberg, AB InBev's Budweiser and Hoegaarden, Simba and White Owl also compete.
parts.WATCH: Watch how it recovers from losses after a company name change forced it to re-register product labels state by state, reports of unpaid dues, and shareholder pressure on management.

quiz.prompt: Which company owns Kingfisher, Bira 91's biggest rival?
What caused Bira 91 to re-register its product labels?
Who controls beer licences and prices in India?

companies.note_30w: Bira 91 is a craft beer brand selling White and Blonde beers to young urban drinkers. It trails Kingfisher. Watch recovery after relabelling troubles and shareholder pressure.

companies.name: Sugar Cosmetics

parts.SELLS: Sugar Cosmetics sells makeup such as lipsticks, kajal, foundations and eyeliners, plus skincare, under the Sugar brand. Its products are designed for Indian skin tones. Young women are its main buyers, through its app, marketplaces and its own stores.
parts.EARNS: It earns by selling products online through its own site, Nykaa, Amazon and quick-commerce apps, and offline through its stores and retail counters. Lip and eye makeup are its biggest categories.
parts.SIZE: One of India's largest homegrown makeup brands, with a large network of retail touchpoints across the country.
parts.RIVALS: Lakme from Hindustan Unilever, Maybelline and L'Oreal, Nykaa Cosmetics, Swiss Beauty, Myglamm and Renee compete with Sugar.
parts.WATCH: Watch its offline expansion, its push to cut losses and turn profitable, and how it fares against fast-growing value brands.

quiz.prompt: What does Sugar Cosmetics mainly sell?
Which HUL brand competes with Sugar?
What are Sugar's biggest categories?

companies.note_30w: Sugar Cosmetics sells makeup made for Indian skin, online and through its own stores. It rivals Lakme, Maybelline and Nykaa Cosmetics. Watch offline expansion and profitability.

companies.name: Plum (Pureplay Skin Sciences)

parts.SELLS: Plum sells vegan skincare, haircare, body care and makeup, including green tea face washes, serums and sunscreens. It also owns the bodycare brand Phy for men. Young urban buyers shop its products online and in stores.
parts.EARNS: It earns by selling products through its own website, marketplaces like Nykaa and Amazon, quick-commerce apps, and its own and partner stores. Skincare is its largest category.
parts.SIZE: One of India's leading homegrown clean-beauty brands, with products sold online across the country and in a growing number of stores.
parts.RIVALS: Mamaearth from Honasa, Minimalist from HUL, The Derma Co, Dot & Key, Foxtale and Lakme compete with Plum.
parts.WATCH: Watch its offline expansion, its moves towards profitability, and reported plans for a stock market listing.

quiz.prompt: What kind of products does Plum mainly sell?
Which is Plum's largest category?
Which Honasa brand competes with Plum?

companies.note_30w: Plum sells vegan skincare, haircare and makeup online and in stores. Skincare is its biggest line. It competes with Mamaearth and Minimalist. Watch offline growth and listing plans.

companies.name: mCaffeine

parts.SELLS: mCaffeine sells caffeine-based personal care products: coffee body scrubs, face washes, shampoos, body washes and under-eye creams. It also owns Hyphen, a skincare brand co-founded with actor Kriti Sanon. Young adults are its main buyers.
parts.EARNS: It earns by selling products through its own site, Nykaa, Amazon, quick-commerce apps and retail stores. Body care and skincare are its largest categories, and online channels bring in most sales.
parts.SIZE: One of India's best-known direct-to-consumer personal care brands, known for building a niche around coffee-based products.
parts.RIVALS: Mamaearth, Plum, Minimalist, The Derma Co, Bombay Shaving Company and global brands like Nivea compete with mCaffeine.
parts.WATCH: Watch its push into offline retail, growth of the Hyphen brand, and its moves towards profitability.

quiz.prompt: Which ingredient defines mCaffeine's products?
Which skincare brand does mCaffeine own?
Where does mCaffeine get most of its sales?

companies.note_30w: mCaffeine sells coffee-based body care and skincare, mostly online, and owns the Hyphen brand. It competes with Mamaearth and Plum. Watch offline expansion and profitability.

companies.name: The Man Company

parts.SELLS: The Man Company sells men's grooming products: beard oils, face washes, body washes, perfumes, deodorants and gift sets. FMCG company Emami is its majority owner. Young urban men are its main buyers, online and in stores.
parts.EARNS: It earns by selling grooming products through its website, marketplaces, quick-commerce apps and retail stores. Fragrances, body care and gift packs are important, with gifting driving festive sales.
parts.SIZE: One of India's better-known direct-to-consumer men's grooming brands, though smaller than Gillette and Nivea Men.
parts.RIVALS: Bombay Shaving Company, Beardo from Marico, Ustraa, Gillette, Nivea Men and Park Avenue compete with The Man Company.
parts.WATCH: Watch how Emami folds it into its wider men's grooming portfolio, its offline distribution push, and new product launches.

quiz.prompt: Which FMCG company is The Man Company's majority owner?
Which Marico brand competes with The Man Company?
What drives The Man Company's festive sales?

companies.note_30w: The Man Company sells men's grooming products online and in stores and is majority owned by Emami. It rivals Bombay Shaving Company and Beardo. Watch offline growth.

companies.name: Bombay Shaving Company

parts.SELLS: Bombay Shaving Company sells razors, shaving kits, beard care, skincare and body care for men, and women's razors and hair removal products. Buyers are young men and women shopping online and in stores.
parts.EARNS: It earns by selling grooming products through its website, Amazon, Nykaa, quick-commerce apps and general trade. Razors and shaving products are its anchor, with skincare a growing share.
parts.SIZE: One of India's largest direct-to-consumer grooming brands, sold across the country.
parts.RIVALS: Gillette from Procter & Gamble is the market leader. Beardo, Ustraa, The Man Company, Philips trimmers and Veet compete in different categories.
parts.WATCH: Watch its expansion into general trade and offline stores, new product categories, and its path to profitability.

quiz.prompt: Which company leads razors against Bombay Shaving Company?
What is Bombay Shaving Company's anchor product line?
Besides men, who does Bombay Shaving Company sell to?

companies.note_30w: Bombay Shaving Company sells razors, beard care and skincare for men and women, online and in stores. Gillette leads the market. Watch offline expansion and profitability.

companies.name: Foxtale

parts.SELLS: Foxtale sells science-led skincare such as sunscreens, vitamin C serums, face washes, moisturisers and acne treatments. Its products target young women and men who want active-ingredient skincare at mass prices.
parts.EARNS: It earns by selling skincare through its website, Nykaa, Amazon and quick-commerce apps. Sunscreens and serums are among its biggest products, and online channels bring in most sales.
parts.SIZE: One of India's fastest-growing young skincare brands, though still smaller than established players.
parts.RIVALS: Minimalist from HUL, The Derma Co from Honasa, Dot & Key from Nykaa, Plum, Deconstruct and Neutrogena compete with Foxtale.
parts.WATCH: Watch its push into offline retail, new product categories, and how it competes with brands now backed by big FMCG and beauty companies.

quiz.prompt: What does Foxtale mainly sell?
Which are among Foxtale's biggest products?
Which HUL-owned brand competes with Foxtale?

companies.note_30w: Foxtale sells active-ingredient skincare like sunscreens and serums, mostly online. It competes with Minimalist, The Derma Co and Dot & Key. Watch offline expansion.

companies.name: Wakefit

parts.SELLS: Wakefit sells mattresses, beds, sofas, wardrobes, tables and home furnishings under its own brand. It started selling mattresses online and now also runs its own stores. It listed on the stock exchanges in December 2025.
parts.EARNS: It earns by designing, making and selling its own products, keeping the margin that would go to distributors. Mattresses are its largest category, with furniture growing. Online sales are big, and its own stores add a growing share.
parts.SIZE: One of India's largest direct-to-consumer home and sleep brands, and a leading online mattress seller.
parts.RIVALS: Sleepwell from Sheela Foam, Kurl-on, Duroflex, The Sleep Company, Pepperfry, IKEA and Godrej Interio compete with Wakefit.
parts.WATCH: Watch its store expansion using money raised in its listing, growth in furniture, and how it handles competition and raw material costs.

quiz.prompt: What is Wakefit's largest product category?
When did Wakefit list on the stock exchanges?
Which Sheela Foam brand competes with Wakefit?

companies.note_30w: Wakefit makes and sells mattresses, furniture and furnishings online and through stores. It listed in December 2025. Rivals include Sleepwell and Duroflex. Watch store expansion.

companies.name: Pepperfry

parts.SELLS: Pepperfry is an online furniture and home goods marketplace selling sofas, beds, dining sets, decor and furnishings. It also has private-label brands and studios where shoppers see products in person. Urban households are its buyers.
parts.EARNS: It earns commissions from third-party sellers and margins on its own private-label furniture. It also earns from services such as delivery and assembly. Furniture is its largest category.
parts.SIZE: One of India's largest online furniture marketplaces, with studios in many Indian cities.
parts.RIVALS: IKEA, Urban Ladder from Reliance Retail, Wakefit, Godrej Interio, Home Centre, Amazon and Flipkart compete with Pepperfry.
parts.WATCH: Watch its push for profitability, expansion of studios into smaller cities, and growth of its private-label brands.

quiz.prompt: What does Pepperfry mainly sell?
How does Pepperfry earn from third-party sellers?
Which global furniture retailer competes with Pepperfry?

companies.note_30w: Pepperfry is an online furniture and home goods marketplace with studios across India. It competes with IKEA, Urban Ladder and Wakefit. Watch profitability and studio expansion.

companies.name: Livspace

parts.SELLS: Livspace offers home interior design and renovation: modular kitchens, wardrobes, false ceilings and full-home interiors. Customers work with its designers, and its partner contractors carry out the work. It operates in India and abroad.
parts.EARNS: It earns from fees and margins on interior projects, including materials, design and installation. Modular kitchens and wardrobes are among its largest project types. Big Indian cities bring in most of its business.
parts.SIZE: One of India's largest home interiors platforms, operating in many Indian cities.
parts.RIVALS: HomeLane, Design Cafe, Bonito Designs, local interior designers and carpenters, and furniture retailers such as Godrej Interio compete with Livspace.
parts.WATCH: Watch its push for profitability, use of AI in design tools, and its expansion in overseas markets.

quiz.prompt: What does Livspace offer?
Which of these is a direct Livspace rival?
Which are among Livspace's largest project types?

companies.note_30w: Livspace designs and builds home interiors such as modular kitchens and wardrobes. It competes with HomeLane and Design Cafe. Watch profitability and overseas expansion.

companies.name: Duroflex

parts.SELLS: Duroflex makes mattresses, pillows, sofas, recliners and beds under the Duroflex and Sleepyhead brands. It sells through dealers, its own stores and online. Households across India are its buyers, especially in the south.
parts.EARNS: It earns by making and selling its own products through dealer stores, company stores and e-commerce. Mattresses are its largest category, and south India is its strongest region.
parts.SIZE: One of India's largest mattress makers and a leading brand in south India.
parts.RIVALS: Sleepwell from Sheela Foam, Kurl-on, Wakefit, The Sleep Company, Springwel and Peps compete with Duroflex.
parts.WATCH: Watch its expansion into north and west India, its online push through Sleepyhead, and reported plans for a stock market listing.

quiz.prompt: What is Duroflex's largest category?
